at sup...@togaware.com"

crs$svm <- svm(BQ2_myvar ~ ., data=crs$dataset[crs$sample,c(1:12,14)],
kernel="rbfdot", probability=TRUE)

doesn't update de Rattle windows.
What's wrong with it ?

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: SVM kernel error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Igor, Richard,

What version of Rattle are you using?

I've tried repeating this in the current beta version (2.3.37) and
don't see the same problem (and it is using ksvm rather than
svm).

Also, Igor, after you do your own "crs$svm <- ..." in the console,
whilst the Rattle textview for the SVM won't be updated, if you
"Evaluate" the SVM in Rattle, it should work okay, using your model.

But of course, we should fix the problem!

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: data size in RATTLE
messages.body_plain:
The data size essentially depends on how much memory and the
architecture. generally, on 32 bit CPUs my rule of thumb had been
about 50,000 rows and 100 columns. 32 bit is limited by the 2GB memory
limit. On 64 bit there is no 2GB limit, and we've loaded in millions
of rows. But then again it depends on what you do with the data, as
copies get made using different commands.

So in short, no built in limitation as such. But in practise, depends
on your situation and what you are doing.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Error runing Random Forests in Rattle
messages.subject_clean: Error runing Random Forests in Rattle
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the bug report Wayne.

The problem is with the randomForest package and is affecting a lot of
Rattle users. The author is aware of the problem. The best solution is
to get an older version of randomForest. For convenience I've put
older versions on the togaware site for people to access:

	http://rattle.togaware.com/randomForest_4.5-23.tar.gz
	http://rattle.togaware.com/randomForest_4.5-20.zip

Regards,
Graham
